newsitem.title: USA: Disney's "101 Dalmatians" at top of U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: Disney's "101 Dalmatians" at top of U.S. box office.

text.p: Walt Disney Co.'s live-action remake of "101 Dalmatians" overcame mixed reviews to shatter U.S. box office records over the Thanksgiving holiday weekend, according to estimates released Sunday.

After opening on Wednesday, the movie earned an estimated $46 million in the five days to Sunday, Disney said. This breaks the previous five-day Thanksgiving record of $43 million held by "Back to the Future 2" since 1989.

The movie also broke the Friday-to-Sunday Thanksgiving record with $34.2 million, while its Friday gross of $13.3 million set a new one-day benchmark for the holiday. Disney's "Toy Story," released last year, held these records with $29.1 million and $11.5 million in box office sales, respectively.
"It's beyond expectations," said Phil Barlow, president of Disney's Buena Vista Pictures distribution unit, noting sales included a large number of reduced-admission children's tickets.

He attributed the film's success in part to strong marketing and merchandising. He also said the children who saw the 1961 animated film are now the parents of today's crop of youngsters, and are keen to see how the movie has evolved.

In the current version, Glenn Close plays the evil fashion world diva Cruella DeVil who hires two crooks to kidnap dalmatians for her latest creation, an authentic Dalmatian coat. Jeff Daniels, Joely Richardson and Joan Plowright also star. The movie averaged $16,464 from 2,794 theaters.
Critics were not overly enthused. According to a Variety survey of reviewers in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and Washington DC, 14 liked it, five did not and 21 were mixed.

The rest of the top five all slipped a notch from last weekend, beginning with "Star Trek: First Contact," which earned $23.4 million over the five days. The movie, released by Viacom Inc.'s Paramount Pictures, has a 10-day gross of $60.7 million and is set to become the most successful of the eight movies in the "Star Trek" franchise.

"Space Jam" followed in third with $17.9 million for the five days, giving it a three-week gross of $67.9 million. The Michael Jordan/Looney Tunes basketball comedy is released by Time Warner Inc.'s Warner Bros.

"Ransom" and "Jingle All The Way," boasting two of the biggest box office draws, were separated by about $100,000. The former, starring Mel Gibson, earned an estimated $17.6 million, while Arnold Schwarzenegger's Christmas comedy came in with $17.5 million.

"Ransom," released by Disney, passed the $100 million mark on Saturday and has an estimated gross after four weeks of $105.3 million. "Jingle All The Way," released by News Corp.'s 20th Century Fox, has $31 million after two weeks.

"The Crucible" debuted on one New York screen to a stellar $98,818. The first major big-screen adaptation of the Arthur Miller play stars Daniel Day-Lewis and Winona Ryder. The movie, released by 20th Century Fox, opens wider over the next few weekends. According to Variety, 20 critics in New York liked "The Crucible," one did not and four were mixed.
